summary: Paul Tedesco worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. under Bernhard Geiger at the University of Vienna (1916–1921), and held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, and Yale (1944–1966).

Paul Theodor Hoffmann was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Grenoble Alpes, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Tübingen, completing his Ph.D. under Richard von Garbe, and later directed the Theaterwissenschaftliches Institut at Hamburg in 1941.

Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Emil Sieg at Göttingen and Kamalakanta Mishra, and held posts at Breslau, Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and theologian who studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He held academic posts at Marburg, TU Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (1955–1962), and Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (circa 1969–1976). Around 1979, he served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chairman at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Paul Whalley was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1857–1864), served in the Bengal Civil Service from 1860 to 1890, and was Secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs (1871–1872).
Paul Wilfred O'Brien was a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley in 1941 and taught at the Pontifical College of St. Pius X from 1958 to 1965.

Paul Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After completing a BA at Sussex and a DPhil at Oxford, he held a fellowship at Wadham College and served as Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at Bristol (~1980–2011).
Paul Wodilla was an Indologist. He studied at Comenius University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1928.

Paul de Lagarde worked in religious studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle under August Tholuck and Friedrich Rückert, later serving as Privatdozent at Halle and Professor at Göttingen from 1869.

Paul-Émile Dumont was an Indologist. He studied at Brussels and Bologna under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè, and also with Willem Caland, Hermann Oldenberg, and Paul Deussen, later teaching at Brussels and serving as professor at Johns Hopkins (1931–1958).

Paula Arai works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her degrees from Kalamazoo College and Harvard, and held faculty posts at Vanderbilt, Carleton College, Louisiana State University, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Paulina Kolata specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After completing her PhD at the University of Manchester, she held research and teaching posts at Manchester, Chester, Copenhagen, and Lund, before joining Harvard as assistant professor in 2025.
Paulina Koniuch works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She earned her bachelor's degree at the University of Warsaw (2017–2020) and became a faculty member there in 2023.

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied in Prague and Rome. He served as a missionary in Malabar, rector at Saint Joseph's Pontifical Seminary, and held posts at Collegio San Pancrazio and the Pontifical Urban University.
Pavankumar Satuluri works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (attested 2024–2025).

Pavel Grintser was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson (~1946–1951). He later held posts at the Gorky Institute of World Literature (~1969–2009) and the Russian State University for the Humanities (~1992–2009).

Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University, St. Petersburg under Robert Lenz, and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held professorships in Sanskrit and Oriental languages at Kazan (1841–1851) and Moscow (1852–1875).

Pavel Konstantinovich Portnyagin was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University in 1932 and served as a translator at the Uzbek Karakul Sheep Breeding Research Institute.

Pavel Poucha was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Hujer, and served as docent at the Oriental Institute from 1948 to 1958.
